answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Each submission hangs on the bridge of a task receipt, and the fable is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. What survives to the river is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The design leans on reciprocity-weighted attestation, capped per identity per epoch, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool.
